tasks.short: Subcontract tree removal and road layout work

steps.what: Subcontract tree removal and road layout after assessing contractors and negotiating terms

tasks.design: The forester assesses contractor suitability and agrees workable site terms using {DOCS}. No separate clerical saving is assumed within this negotiation task.
tasks.previous_blocker: Capability, access and commercial terms depend on the site and contractor.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing documents can support the discussion without replacing it.
tasks.still_hard: Balancing road layout, removal methods and enforceable commitments.
tasks.human_edge: Evaluate people and negotiate feasible obligations.
tasks.altitude: Own contractor performance and site outcomes.

evidence.claim: Site-specific forestry subcontract negotiation remains a human judgement task in this design.

assumptions: The baseline covers selection, negotiation and agreement rather than a separate repetitive contract-entry task.
No new automation is introduced, so no additional system upkeep is required.
unknowns: Local purchasing authority and contractor qualification process
research_questions: How much observed subcontracting time is repetitive entry rather than negotiation?

incremental.description: No new tool or process upkeep

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net saving 0. No negotiation time is removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Analyze forest conditions and species growth

steps.what: Define forest comparisons and prepare measured growth and species observations
Calculate descriptive summaries for the specified forest comparisons
Analyze growth patterns and distinguish observed associations from causal explanations

tasks.design: Configure reusable descriptive tables in {SPREADSHEET} after the forester defines the comparison and prepares observations. The forester checks anomalies and writes the ecological interpretation in {DOCS}; the workbook makes no causal recommendation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Measurements and species categories may be inconsistent across plots and years.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing spreadsheet formulas can repeat a specified descriptive calculation.
tasks.still_hard: Sampling bias, confounding and long observation periods.
tasks.human_edge: Decide what comparisons mean for forest management.

ambition.what: Revisit comparisons when comparable new measurements become available, subject to extra fieldwork.

tasks.altitude: Own reproducible comparisons and their ecological limitations.

evidence.claim: Copernicus supplies land-cover and water context; that does not establish tree-level growth effects or labour savings.
A workbook can repeat specified descriptive calculations; the proposed time effect is unmeasured.

assumptions: The forester produces plot ID, observation date, species, measured growth, yield or seed outcome, units, missingness and selected condition fields in s1; its 40 hours includes extraction, capture and validation.
Unclear units, incomparable samples or missing measures return to manual investigation; they are not guessed or classified automatically.
Use native spreadsheet functions before considering another application.
Eight extra focal hours per 100 baseline hours cover formula checks and changed measurement definitions.
New field surveys are outside this analysis baseline and create no claimed saving.
unknowns: Actual share spent calculating descriptive tables
research_questions: Do repeated studies contain enough identical calculation work to exceed capture and maintenance costs?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=75; gross 25 minus 8 upkeep gives central net 17%. The stated 0-5% pilot range discounts the unverified calculation share and potentially expensive data cleaning; already automated studies save zero.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Conduct forest care education with demonstrations and audience questions

tasks.design: Keep the forester responsible for demonstrations, explanation and questions. Existing materials in {DOCS} support delivery without assuming a separate drafting workload.
tasks.previous_blocker: Learning depends on audience understanding and local examples.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing education materials can support a live session.
tasks.still_hard: Correct misconceptions and adapt explanations in real time.
tasks.human_edge: Earn attention and make practical forest care understandable.
tasks.altitude: Develop effective public understanding of conservation.

evidence.claim: Live practical conservation teaching retains its human delivery time in this design.

assumptions: This baseline is conducting the program, including practical explanation, rather than an invented slide-writing phase.
Use existing document materials; no new tool or upkeep is introduced.
unknowns: Audience access needs and program format
research_questions: What part of observed program work, if any, is repetitive material preparation?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net 0. Delivery and audience interaction remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Assess timber offered by landowners and resolve ownership and harvesting constraints
Procure timber by negotiating and agreeing authorized purchase terms with landowners

tasks.design: The forester assesses the timber and negotiates within existing purchasing authority, using {DOCS} for supporting records. Ownership questions and unusual terms go through the existing human process.
tasks.previous_blocker: Timber quality, access and owner expectations vary by transaction.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing purchase records support negotiation without replacing judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Verify rights and agree commercially workable terms.
tasks.human_edge: Balance valuation, site conditions and the owner's relationship.
tasks.altitude: Own the quality and reliability of timber supply.

evidence.claim: Timber purchase judgement and owner negotiation are retained without an unverified automation saving.

assumptions: The focal forester has existing authority or obtains it through the current process; authority is not created by software.
No repeated clerical stage is assumed merely because purchase documents exist.
Existing document tools suffice, with no new automation maintenance.
unknowns: Purchasing limits and ownership verification requirements
research_questions: Does actual timber procurement contain a material recurring administrative stage outside negotiation?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net saving 0. Assessment and agreement retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Own forest decisions, reproducible evidence and trusted supplier and community relationships.
reach: Support ecological analysts with validated descriptive comparisons
Work with procurement advisers on unusual timber terms
role.ambitious_version: A forester who uses repeatable calculations to strengthen field judgement while protecting time for contractors, landowners and public education.
